topic: PhoneBuddy SDK: Embeddable Rust LLM Agent Engine for iOS and Android

key_points: Primary source: APUS-AI-Lab open-sourced PhoneBuddySDK on 2026-08-18 under Apache-2.0; core is pure Rust (1.36 MB Rust vs 36 KB C) with a C ABI (phone_buddy.h) plus first-class Swift (PhoneBuddy.swift) and Kotlin (NativeAgent.kt + JNI) wrappers.

Explicitly derived from xAI's open-source desktop harness xai-org/grok-build — the NOTICE file lists the adaptations: replacing std::process / tokio::process with pure-Rust BusyBox applets, an in-memory Tokio task manager for subagents, rustls-ring TLS, and new C FFI / Swift / Kotlin layers.
Core loop: autonomous planning plus a ReAct tool loop with doom-loop detection, history compactor, session store, in-memory subagent orchestration, cron-style scheduler and task monitor.

Tooling runs entirely in-process: jailed file sandbox (root_dir jailing, path-traversal prevention, read_file/write_file/edit_file/list_dir/grep), a pure-Rust virtual POSIX shell (cat, head, tail, ls, wc, sort, uniq, find, echo, mkdir, rm, cp, mv, du), and an embedded JavaScript sandbox via boa_engine (run_script) for computation and CSV/JSON manipulation.

LLM transport supports three wire protocols (responses with SSE streaming, chat_completions, messages), HTTP/2 streaming over rustls-ring, and an LlmMode::Host mode that delegates inference to an on-device model such as llama.cpp / llama.rn through PbLlmRequestCallback.

Notable claim: 1:1 client-profile emulation of xAI Grok Build, OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code, replicating their exact HTTP headers, thinking signatures and JSON wire schemas from a mobile app.
The README asserts the SDK 'Passes Apple App Store and Google Play app sandbox security reviews with zero permission escalations' — a project assertion, not a documented review outcome.
Independent audit (published 2026-08-23) of main commit c661ba0 — the strongest critical source on the project.

Confirms statically that the core crates contain no std::process, tokio::process or child-process launch path; verifies path jailing, bounded JavaScript, tool timeouts, cancellation token propagation and Swift/Kotlin/C integration.

Concrete verified limits: run_script runs Boa with a 20-million-iteration cap; built-in and host tools are wrapped in a 120-second timeout; the doom-loop guard nudges after 8 identical calls and breaks after 16; cooperative cancellation propagates through the in-memory task manager.

Caveats that the marketing does not state: 174 Rust tests are defined but there is no public GitHub Actions workflow and no Android instrumentation suite; the auditor could not execute the tests because the host lacked a Rust toolchain.
The v0.1.2 release pointed at an earlier commit than the audited main, so main-branch findings must not be attributed to the release package without retesting.
No public App Store or Google Play review record was found anywhere; the 'passed review' claim remains unverified.

Legal framing worth quoting: Apple Guideline 2.5.2 restricts downloading/installing/executing code that introduces or changes app functionality, and an embedded JavaScript interpreter does not make that policy question disappear; Google Play prohibits downloading dex/JAR/.so outside Play but allows VM/interpreter code under conditions.

Analysis piece framing PhoneBuddySDK against every prior mobile-agent route: cloud chat apps (ChatGPT/Doubao) cannot touch local files, system assistants (Siri) are closed to third parties, and remote-control/cloud-sandbox agents offload work off the device.

Central insight: PhoneBuddySDK 'didn't fake a command-line terminal to trick the underlying model' — it re-implemented each agent capability in code and wrapped every operation in a controlled execution fence instead of emulating a shell.

Emphasizes the in-process trade-off: the agent's reach is bounded by the host app's own permissions, so an agent inside a photos app cannot touch system contacts; that same boundary is what makes it auditable.

Argues the desktop-to-mobile task-completion gap is an execution-environment problem, not a model problem: the same LLM delivers results an order of magnitude apart between a desktop harness and a phone chatbot.

The closest direct alternative: antgroup/Napaxi is a mobile-native agent SDK (Rust core, ★33, GPL-3.0, created 2026-07-01, last pushed 2026-09-30) explicitly framed as 'shared Rust agent runtime + thin mobile SDK adapters'.
Flutter is the first complete adapter and demo target, with Android and iOS adapters sharing one Core API boundary — a different portability bet than PhoneBuddySDK's C-ABI-first approach.

Feature overlap: sessions, workspace state, storage, tools, skills, MCP, platform hooks, background execution, and adapter contracts; host apps keep ownership of UI, accounts, model configuration and product policy.

Differentiators: xApp / xAgent / xChannel connectivity (cross-app interaction, on-device multi-agent collaboration, IM/Bluetooth/headset/vehicle channels) and an explicit MCP surface that PhoneBuddySDK does not advertise.
Licensing contrast matters for commercial adopters: Napaxi is GPL-3.0 (copyleft) while PhoneBuddySDK is Apache-2.0 (permissive).

PalmClaw (arXiv 2607.13027, 2026-07-14) is the research-lab counterpoint: a native on-device agent framework that keeps sessions, memory, skills, tools and the agent loop on the phone and exposes device capabilities as typed 'device tools' with explicit arguments and defined execution boundaries.
Reported results: 11.5% relative improvement in task success and a 94.9% reduction in completion time versus the strongest baseline, with lower setup burden.

Positions the split in mobile agents: GUI-action agents (tap/swipe/type) produce long interface-dependent sequences and cannot access device capabilities directly, whereas device-tool agents get explicit, auditable boundaries — the same argument PhoneBuddySDK makes from the SDK side.

Release-day coverage (2026-08-18) summarizing the same feature set: pure Rust for iOS and Android, C FFI plus Swift/Kotlin bindings, sandboxed runtime, tool-calling loop, streaming LLM transport, JS scripting sandbox and in-memory subagent orchestration.
Records Apache-2.0 licensing and the Rust 1.94+ toolchain requirement, plus a 36-star snapshot — useful as a point-in-time adoption baseline.

Verified static safety limits: 20,000,000-iteration cap on the Boa JS sandbox, 120-second timeout wrapper on built-in and host tools, doom-loop guard nudging at 8 identical calls and breaking at 16, plus cooperative cancellation tokens.

angles: The in-process bet: why 'no child processes' is an architectural requirement on iOS/Android rather than an optimization — and how porting xAI's grok-build harness down to a single app process is the real story, not the feature list.

Compliance, not marketing: the repo claims it passes App Store and Play review, but no public review record exists; dissect Guideline 2.5.2 and the Google Play interpreter exception, and explain why an embedded Boa JS engine keeps the policy question open.

Desktop-class harness maturity on a phone: compare PhoneBuddySDK's planner / doom-loop detector / history compactor / subagent manager against GUI-automation mobile agents that can only tap and swipe.

Rust as the mobile agent substrate: one core with C FFI + Swift + Kotlin bindings versus platform-native rewrites — including the practical cost (Rust 1.94+, NDK r25+, 4 target toolchains) and the 1.36 MB Rust / 36 KB C footprint split.
Read the licenses before you ship: PhoneBuddySDK is Apache-2.0 while its closest rival Napaxi is GPL-3.0 — a decisive difference for closed-source mobile apps.

The unfinished verification stack: 174 tests defined but no CI, no Android instrumentation suite, and a v0.1.2 release pointing at a pre-audit commit — what a team must independently validate before trusting the sandbox claims.

Bring-your-own-model vs hosted frontier models: LlmMode::Host delegates to llama.cpp / llama.rn on NPU-class devices, while the default path emulates Grok Build / Codex / Claude Code client profiles against remote APIs.
